segments.text: Completing the first classical collection of the Encyclopedia of Triangle Centers, X nineteen is the Clawson Point, discovered by John Wentworth Clawson in nineteen twenty-five: the homothetic center and perspector of the orthic triangle H sub a, H sub b, H sub c and the extangents triangle, as well as the perspector of the orthic and extouch triangles.

segments.text: Its trilinear coordinates are simply tangent A, to tangent B, to tangent C— matching the barycentric coordinates of the Orthocenter X four! Consequently, its barycentric coordinates are a tangent A, to b tangent B, to c tangent C. On the central lines layer, X nineteen lies on the Orthocenter–Mittenpunkt–Spieker line through X four, X nine, and X ten.

segments.text: Under functional relations, X nineteen is the isogonal conjugate of X sixty-three, the isotomic conjugate of X three hundred four, and concludes the nineteen foundational centers of the ETC.
